resources.string: Navigation shell only — not implemented yet.
Host profiles arrive in the next phase. Nothing here connects to a server yet, and no account or sign-in is required to use local profiles.
When host profiles exist, tapping a host opens its session. Until then, the session screen below is a labelled preview only.
Host profiles are stored on this device only. Credentials are encrypted with the device keystore and never stored in plain text.
Leave blank on edit to keep the stored password
Paste the PEM private key here
The passphrase is never stored. It will be asked again when you connect.
Delete %1$s? Its stored credential will be deleted too. This cannot be undone.
Select a host to connect to
Add a host first, then return here to connect to it.
Leave blank if your key has no passphrase
This server has never been seen before. Only trust it if you expected this fingerprint — for example, from the server administrator.

This server presents a different key than the one previously trusted. This can mean the server was reinstalled — or that someone is intercepting the connection. Only trust it if you have verified the new fingerprint another way.
Type here — keys go to the shell as you type
The following text will be sent to the shell exactly as shown, including any newlines. Only send it if you trust it. Text: %1$s
File browsing uses SFTP, which only works where the server offers an SFTP subsystem. It is not universal file access to any Windows machine.
Delete %1$s? This cannot be undone. A non-empty directory cannot be deleted here.
A file named %1$s already exists in this directory. Overwrite it, or upload under a new name?
Create a button for the selected host. Buttons are stored per host and never run when created, selected, or when a screen opens.
Select a host to manage its command buttons
Insert only — place text in the terminal, do not run it
Execute one — run a single command in the live terminal
Steps, one per line, in order
Variables, one per line: name or name=default
Buttons must not store credentials. A button that looks like it contains a secret cannot be saved.

Sequences send steps in order with a short pause between them. They do not stop automatically on an error, because an interactive shell does not report per-step results to the app. Use Stop to prevent further steps from being sent.
Open session to use these buttons
Preview — exactly what will be inserted or sent:
Insert only: this text will be placed in the terminal input and will NOT run until you press Enter yourself.
This command will be sent to the live terminal when you tap Run.
These steps will be sent to the live terminal in order when you tap Run sequence.

Shell not confirmed for this host — parameter values below are quoted for a POSIX shell. If this host actually runs cmd.exe, that quoting does not protect values. Set the host’s shell in Environment and save before running parameterised buttons.
Parameterised commands are blocked while this host’s shell is not confirmed. Set the host’s shell in Environment and save, then try again.
This command was prepared for a different shell. Open the button again to prepare it for the current shell.
This command was flagged as potentially destructive, privilege-escalating, or disruptive. Detection is a heuristic and can miss dangerous commands, so check the command yourself before running it.
Sequence stopped after step %1$d of %2$d. Steps already sent keep running on the server.
Insert places text in the terminal without running it. Run sends it to the live terminal. Nothing runs until you tap Run or Insert.
These settings belong to this host only. The server may ignore environment requests, and login profiles or server policies can override them — nothing here guarantees a variable reaches the shell.
Environment values are encrypted on this device and never shown. Editing a variable requires typing its value again.
Changes apply on the next connection, not to a session that is already running.

For a terminal session, this directory is entered once with a visible cd command when the shell starts. For file browsing, it is the starting directory for POSIX paths only. Command buttons are never changed by this setting.
Chosen with the system file picker. Downloads for this host write straight into this folder. No broad storage access is used.
Folder permission could not be kept, so the folder was not saved.
Variables are requested from the server when a terminal session starts. The server may accept or ignore each one; the session screen reports which were accepted.
No environment variables for this host.
Variable name must not be blank.
Value (may contain a secret — it is stored encrypted)
Type the new value (the stored value is never shown)
Acceptance means the server did not reject the request. Login profiles can still override a value — check in the shell if a command behaves unexpectedly.
Downloads for this host go straight into its local folder (see the host environment settings).
Tunnels run on their own connection, separate from the terminal session. Pick a host, configure its tunnels, jump chain, and proxy, then start them.
By default every tunnel binds to loopback (127.0.0.1) only, so it is reachable only from this device.
No hosts yet. Add a host first.
Allow non-loopback bind — exposes this port to the local network. Use only on trusted networks.
Delete the tunnel %1$s? Its configuration will be removed.
No jump hosts. Connections go directly to the target.
Remove all jump hosts for this host? The target host itself is not affected.
A SOCKS proxy operator can see the target hostname and port and the timing of the connection, though not the encrypted SSH content. Only use a proxy you trust.
No tunnels yet. Add one below.
Ports must be numbers between 1 and 65535.
sshj 0.40.0 has no SOCKS server, so there is nothing safe to offer here.
No standard-library support; a hand-written CONNECT handshake is unproven and is not shipped.
sshj has no ProxyCommand support, and bridging a local process to a socket is unproven here.
SOCKS authentication would need the JVM-global Authenticator, which would leak credentials across connections.

Remote desktop is conditional, not promised. RDP is blocked by the prompt 12 proof gate: no RDP connection has been demonstrated yet. VNC has a protocol core implemented but no session yet: it has never connected to a real VNC server. See the rows below for the exact state and what would unblock each.

Blocked by the prompt 12 proof-of-concept gate: no RDP connection has been demonstrated yet. FreeRDP is the only candidate, but it ships no Android library — its native code must be built from source with the Android NDK, and this environment has no NDK, no CI build, and no Windows endpoint to test against.

Candidate: FreeRDP 3.x, actively maintained, with an Android port updated in recent releases. Its core is Apache-2.0; the full licence inventory for the exact linked components is still open and must come from the FreeRDP source tree at integration time.

What would unblock it: a CI machine with the NDK that builds the FreeRDP native libraries for the target ABIs, a licence inventory for the exact linked components, and a real connection to a compatible Windows endpoint — Pro, Enterprise, or Education with Remote Desktop enabled. Windows Home cannot host a Remote Desktop session.

Protocol core implemented, session not yet available: a pure-Kotlin RFB client core is in the app — protocol versions 3.3, 3.7 and 3.8, No Authentication and VNC Authentication, and Raw, CopyRect, RRE, CoRRE and Hextile framebuffer decoding — with unit tests for the protocol logic. It has never connected to a real VNC server.

Blocked by the prompt 13 proof-of-concept gate for a session: the pack requires a proven connection against a controlled compatible server before full integration, and this environment has no controlled Linux VNC server, no device, and no CI run to prove against. Tight, ZRLE, TRLE and encrypted authentication (VeNCrypt, TLS, X.509) are not implemented and are refused cleanly, never silently downgraded. VNC Authentication itself is weak by design and must only be used on a trusted network or through an SSH tunnel.

What would unblock it: a controlled Linux VNC server (for example TigerVNC or x11vnc) with documented version, authentication and encodings, a real connection from a device build proving the handshake, authentication and framebuffer updates end to end, and a session screen with scaling, pointer and keyboard input — only then a connect button.
Move hosts between devices with a backup file. Only one format is supported: a TermBridge backup (JSON, version 1). Other files, including PuTTY files, are rejected.

Never exported: trusted host keys (trust must be re-established on first connection after import) and the local folder on this device (a folder choice does not work on another device). Nothing here runs a command or trusts a host key automatically.

Without secrets, the file holds hosts, command buttons, working directories, tunnels, and proxies — but no password, private key, or environment value. After import, credentials and environment values must be entered again.

The passphrase is never stored. If you lose it, the encrypted backup cannot be opened — there is no recovery. It must be at least 8 characters. Anyone with this file can try passphrases offline, without the app\'s protection — use a long, unique passphrase.
Hosts: %1$d, command buttons: %2$d, tunnels: %3$d, environment variables: %4$d.
This backup is encrypted and was opened with your passphrase.
This backup contains credentials, which will be stored encrypted on this device.
Already on this device (same server and username):
Replace the existing hosts listed above

Without this option, conflicting hosts are skipped and the existing hosts are left untouched. With it, the existing host and its buttons, settings, and tunnels are replaced — but its credential is replaced only when this backup contains one.
This will replace %1$d existing host(s). A credential is replaced only when this backup contains one; otherwise the existing credential is kept.
Settings that change behaviour arrive with the features they control. For now this screen only leads to diagnostics and about information, and the app follows the system theme.
Screenshots and screen recordings are blocked in this app, so terminal content cannot appear in the Recents overview. This also means you cannot screenshot the app yourself.
Active sessions: 1 live session (see the Session screen)

TermBridge is an independent app for managing remote servers over SSH. It is not affiliated with any other terminal or remote-access product, and it contains no copied branding, code, or assets from one.

Jetpack Compose (BOM 2024.09.00), Navigation Compose 2.8.0, Kotlin Coroutines 1.8.1, Room 2.6.1, sshj 0.40.0, kotlinx-serialization-json 1.7.3, Material Icons Extended (Compose BOM 2024.09.00), and the AndroidX core, lifecycle, and activity libraries — all Apache License 2.0. Test-only dependencies (JUnit, Espresso, Compose UI test) are not shipped in the app.
Tap to cycle. Applies to the next connection.
Prevents the display from sleeping while the terminal is open.
Sends a heartbeat so idle connections are not dropped. Applies to the next connection.
Hides terminal content from screenshots and the Recents preview.
Command buttons that paste or run for you
Enter a host, user@host:port, or an ssh command.
A server key is remembered here after you trust it on first connection.
%1$s will be treated as a new server and you will be asked to verify its fingerprint again.
Connections you make appear here. Terminal output is never stored.
Looks for SSH (22), VNC (5900) and RDP (3389) on your local subnet only.
No local network address available. Connect to Wi-Fi first.
A short haptic tick when the server rings the bell.
Too many attempts. Try again in %1$d seconds.
On. Asked after the app has been in the background for 30 seconds.
Keeps casual users out of an unlocked phone. Saved credentials are encrypted by the Android Keystore either way.
Not available on this device, or none enrolled.

VNC is not encrypted. Use it on a trusted network, or through a VPN or SSH tunnel.
Windows Remote Desktop (RDP) is not supported yet. For Windows, install a VNC server (for example TightVNC, UltraVNC or RealVNC) and connect to it here.
